presentingComplaint: High fever with rigors, burning micturition and worsening left loin pain for 3 days, now drowsy with cold clammy peripheries for 6 hours.
history: Type 2 diabetic (18 years, HbA1c 8.9%) with long-standing benign prostatic obstruction and a post-void residual of ~180 mL on prior scans. Two episodes of febrile UTI in the past year; a urine culture 4 months ago grew an ESBL-producing E. coli treated with a course of oral fosfomycin. No indwelling catheter. Over 3 days he developed dysuria, frequency and left flank pain with rigors; today the family found him confused, with reduced urine output and cool mottled limbs, prompting emergency presentation.
examination: Toxic, drowsy but rousable (GCS 14). Warm-to-cool peripheries with delayed capillary refill (4 s), mottled knees. Marked left costovertebral-angle tenderness. Suprapubic fullness, palpable bladder; per-rectal exam shows a smoothly enlarged, non-tender prostate. Chest clear, abdomen otherwise soft. No rash.

labs.urinalysis: leucocyte esterase +++, nitrite positive, >100 WBC/hpf, many bacteria

imaging: Bedside/renal ultrasound: mild left pelvicalyceal dilatation, no obstructing calculus; grossly trabeculated bladder with 190 mL post-void residual and enlarged prostate. CT KUB (after stabilisation): left-sided perinephric fat stranding consistent with pyelonephritis in a functionally obstructed lower tract; no abscess or emphysematous change.
microbiology: Two sets of blood cultures and a catheter-obtained urine culture sent before antibiotics. Urine and one blood culture set grew Escherichia coli >10^5 CFU/mL; sensitivities returned at 48 h: ESBL-producer, resistant to ceftriaxone, ciprofloxacin and co-trimoxazole; susceptible to meropenem, ertapenem, amikacin and nitrofurantoin (urine only).
differentialDiagnoses: Complicated UTI / urosepsis with septic shock (obstructive uropathy + diabetes)
finalDiagnosis: Complicated urinary tract infection (obstructive uropathy and diabetes) with ESBL E. coli bacteraemic urosepsis and septic shock
citations: European Association of Urology (EAU) — Urological Infections — 2023
Surviving Sepsis Campaign — Sepsis and Septic Shock — 2021
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e — Urinary Tract Infections and Pyelonephritis
stewardship: This is a complicated UTI with septic shock and organ dysfunction in a host with a documented prior ESBL E. coli — the highest-risk category. After two blood cultures and a urine culture, give a broad empiric carbapenem (meropenem 1 g IV 8-hourly, renally dose-adjusted) within the first hour alongside 30 mL/kg balanced crystalloid and early noradrenaline to maintain MAP >=65 mmHg; a carbapenem is guideline-concordant empiric cover here because prior ESBL colonisation plus septic shock makes beta-lactam/beta-lactamase-inhibitor cover unreliable. Source control is central: relieve lower-tract obstruction with a urethral/suprapubic catheter and ensure the mildly obstructed upper tract drains. Once susceptibilities confirm a carbapenem-susceptible ESBL E. coli at 48 h and the patient is off vasopressors and improving, de-escalate from meropenem to ertapenem 1 g IV once daily to complete a 10-14 day course for complicated UTI, reserving broader agents. Avoid nitrofurantoin (no tissue/bloodstream cover) and fluoroquinolones (resistant, plus tendinopathy/QT risk).
contraindications: Nitrofurantoin inappropriate for pyelonephritis/bacteraemia and contraindicated at eGFR-reducing AKI
Fluoroquinolones inappropriate given documented resistance and adverse-effect profile
Nephrotoxin exposure (NSAIDs, contrast without hydration) to be minimised during AKI
Metformin should be held during AKI and lactic acidosis
edgeCases: If ultrasound had shown hydronephrosis with an obstructing stone, emergency decompression (ureteric stent/nephrostomy) would take priority over antibiotic choice
Emphysematous pyelonephritis in a poorly controlled diabetic can mimic this and needs urgent CT and possible drainage/nephrectomy
Persistent bacteraemia or failure to improve at 72 h should prompt search for renal/prostatic abscess
expectedMaiK: Complicated UTI with septic shock in a diabetic with obstructive uropathy and prior ESBL warrants immediate cultures, empiric carbapenem cover, sepsis resuscitation and source control, then culture-directed de-escalation to ertapenem.

investigations: Blood cultures x2 and urine culture before antibiotics

regressionAssertions: Recognises septic shock (hypotension + lactate + vasopressor need) with organ dysfunction (AKI, thrombocytopenia)
Recommends blood and urine cultures before empiric antibiotics
Empiric cover is a carbapenem given prior ESBL plus septic shock
De-escalates from meropenem to ertapenem once ESBL E. coli susceptibilities return
Includes source control of lower-tract obstruction
